evidence_limits: Synthetic product brief and rendered example only.
No representative user research was used.
preserve: Current product data and selection behavior.
Purchase control and its accessible name.

findings.location: fictional product detail page, price and purchase panel
findings.evidence_observed: In the synthetic flow, delivery cost appears only after adding the item to the cart.
findings.probable_impact: Shoppers may postpone a decision or encounter an unexpected cost; this effect is a hypothesis, not a measured outcome.

confidence.reason: The sequence is visible in the supplied synthetic flow; user impact is a hypothesis.

findings.next_step: Ask the product owner for approved shipping-estimate rules, then show an estimate near the price if authorized.
findings.acceptance_criteria: The product page states how delivery cost is determined before cart, using approved shipping rules; keyboard and mobile checks pass.
findings.requires_external_data_or_approval: Product owner must confirm shipping rules.

findings.location: fictional product detail page, option selector
findings.evidence_observed: The option labels contain internal paper codes without an explanation in the synthetic brief.
findings.probable_impact: First-time shoppers may not compare options confidently; comprehension is untested.

confidence.reason: Code labels are observed, but shopper comprehension was not tested.

findings.next_step: Request approved plain-language attributes and validate comprehension with representative shoppers.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Every option exposes an approved, understandable attribute without changing the underlying product value.
findings.requires_external_data_or_approval: Approved attribute names and user validation are required.

handoff.summary: After the user approves individual findings and any required external inputs are available, implement only approved findings and verify their acceptance criteria.
